raw_response.adversarial_critique:
Claude's stored row for S149 fails adversarial audit on three independent fronts: (1) obvious abstract-only numerical extraction that omits explicitly printed SEs/95% CIs and propagates an internal outcome-label swap in the paper; (2) an obsolete `reasoned non-fit` justification that contradicts the A21 synthesis-family definitions; and (3) unflagged Criterion 2 scope and data-integrity red flags requiring PI review.

1. Abstract-Only Extraction & Outcome Mislabelling: Claude copied the multi-outcome prose summary straight from the Abstract (p. 1) into `effect_estimate` and left `lower_CI`, `upper_CI`, and `standard_error` completely blank, despite Table 8 (p. 10) printing exact SEs, t-statistics, p-values, and 95% CIs for every PSM outcome. Worse, because Claude did not cross-check Results Section 3.7 (p. 9) or Table 8 (p. 10), Claude uncritically repeated the Abstract's claim that VWSC participation `"improved toilet functionality by 24.8%"`, whereas Section 3.7 and Table 8 explicitly report `+24.8%` (SE = 5.2, 95% CI [14.6%, 35.0%]) for **Water Source Functionality** and `+19.3%` (SE = 4.7, 95% CI [10.1%, 28.5%]) for **Toilet Usage Rate** (with no "toilet functionality" row in Table 8 at all). Claude also bundled a non-governance physical-geography covariate (`distance to water source`, standardized beta = 0.62 from Table 2, p. 6) and a non-Criterion 4 health outcome (`illness incidence` -12.7%) into the same string, while overlooking Table 5's (p. 8) probit marginal effect for `VWSC awareness campaign` on consistent toilet usage (+15.8 percentage points, SE = 0.047, 95% CI [0.066, 0.250]).

2. Flawed `Reasoned Non-Fit` Rationale (`questionable_could_fit_family_ABC`): Claude's `provenance_note` justifies leaving `synthesis_family` blank by citing `PROJECT_SPEC.md S8`'s narrow pre-A21 framing of Family B as strictly `"provider-side 'bureaucratic assistance' (which describes officials helping applicants navigate procedure, not citizens participating in local governance bodies)"`. Under A21, however, Family B was explicitly broadened to encompass community participation, outreach/assistance, and trust mechanisms (and Family A covers local governance arrangements). Even on Claude's own narrow provider-outreach framing, Table 5 (p. 8) directly estimates committee-led outreach (`VWSC awareness campaign` -> +15.8 pp consistent toilet usage). Thus, if S149 remains included in the review, excluding it from Family B as a `reasoned non-fit` is inconsistent with A21.

3. Narrow Criterion 2 Scope & Study-Integrity Flags (`borderline_flag_for_pi`): Applying the `2026-10-13 / 2026-10-14` CK narrow Criterion 2 standard (`A24/A26/A28`), S149 sits on a sharp eligibility knife-edge (`E03` risk). While VWSCs are formal decentralized local governance committees under India's Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin, no legal rule, statutory mandate, gender quota, tariff, or administrative eligibility rule varies across the 16 sampled villages in Odisha (mandating 50% women's representation in VWSCs is proposed only as a future policy recommendation in Section 4.5b, p. 14). Instead, the empirical exposure is a behavioural/empowerment composite (`Women's Agency Score 0-10`: attendance 20%, speaking time 30%, decision influence 30%, leadership 20%; p. 4) binarized at an unstated cutoff. Moreover, the paper exhibits severe reporting/validity defects: every mathematical equation in Sections 2.4-2.6 (pp. 3-5) failed to render in the published PDF (`disp lay-eq- Equa`, `inli ne-eq-IEq1`), the PSM analysis treats village-level VWSC participation across just 16 villages (400 households) without reporting the propensity model, matched N, balance diagnostics, or village-cluster inference, and the Abstract/Conclusion contradict Table 8 on which WASH facility improved by 24.8%. The PI should determine whether de facto VWSC participation / awareness campaigns pass narrow Criterion 2 (in which case S149 belongs in Family B with corrected Table 8/Table 5 statistics) or fail under `E03`/quality screening.

raw_response.number_verification_detail:
Multiple substantive discrepancies exist between Claude's stored `effect_sizes.csv` row (extracted solely from the Abstract on p. 1) and the full-text statistical tables:
1. Omitted Printed Precision Statistics (`lower_CI`, `upper_CI`, `standard_error` all left blank `""`): Table 8 (PDF p. 10) explicitly prints SEs, t-statistics, p-values, and 95% CIs for every PSM outcome:
   - Water Source Functionality: ATT = +24.8%, Std. Error = 5.2, t-stat = 4.77, p < 0.001, 95% CI [14.6%, 35.0%].
   - Toilet Usage Rate (omitted completely by Claude): ATT = +19.3%, Std. Error = 4.7, t-stat = 4.11, p < 0.001, 95% CI [10.1%, 28.5%].
   - Water Collection Time: ATT = -31.4 min, Std. Error = 8.6, t-stat = -3.65, p < 0.001, 95% CI [-48.3, -14.5] (raw negative sign = beneficial time reduction).
   - Diarrhoea Incidence (non-C4 health outcome): ATT = -12.7%, Std. Error = 3.8, t-stat = -3.34, p = 0.001, 95% CI [-20.2%, -5.2%].
2. Severe Outcome-Label Contradiction (+24.8% mislabelled): Claude recorded `"VWSC participation improved toilet functionality by 24.8%"` from the Abstract (p. 1; repeated in Conclusion p. 15). However, Results Section 3.7 (p. 9) and Table 8 (p. 10) report +24.8% for `Water Source Functionality`, whereas the sanitation outcome in Table 8 is `Toilet Usage Rate` (+19.3%); there is no `toilet functionality` row in Table 8.
3. Bundled Non-Governance Predictor & Missing Unstandardized Stats: Claude appended `distance to water source (beta=0.62, p<0.001)`, which is the standardized beta (`Std. Β = 0.62`) for physical distance (km) in the OLS time-poverty regression (Table 2, p. 6; unstandardized B = 4.82, Robust SE = 0.67, t = 7.19, 95% CI [3.50, 6.14]), not a governance treatment effect.
4. Omitted Committee Outreach Estimate: Claude missed Table 5 (p. 8), where `VWSC awareness campaign` increases `Consistent Toilet Usage` by dy/dx = 0.158 (+15.8 percentage points; Delta-method SE = 0.047, z = 3.36, p = 0.001, 95% CI [0.066, 0.250]).
5. Sample Size & Unit-of-Assignment Ambiguity: Stored `sample_size = "400 households"` matches total surveyed households (N = 400 across 16 villages, 25/village; pp. 3, 5) and `comparator_definition` states `"Non-participating households/women"`, whereas Section 3.7 (p. 9) defines treatment at the village level (`"villages with active women's participation in VWSCs"`, only 16 villages total) and the paper never reports the post-matching sample size or cluster adjustment.
